title: moveItem: the rows on screen -> where the finger presses and where it releases, or why the step fails
description: Shared vector for the moveItem action (schemas/actions.schema.json; ticket jui-collection-drag-to-reorder). Run by the three drivers against their own gesture planning, before any gesture is made.

Coordinates are the screen's (points on iOS, dp on Android, CSS pixels on the web), y downward; edgeMargin and listMargin are in the same units, so a margin is the same distance under the finger on every platform. A rect is [x, y, width, height]. rows maps an address (<id>_item_<n>) to the rects found for it: one rect is a row; none (absent) is a row not drawn; two or more is an address that repeats (several sections).

press: the centre of the handle's rect when the step gives `handle` (the reorderHandle id; the case's handle is the rect of that element found inside the from row, null when none was found), else the centre of the from row.

release: x is the press's x (the finger moves straight up or down); y is where the dragged row's centre lands — the to row's top + 3/4 of its height when to > from, + 1/4 when to < from — plus the press's offset from the from row's centre (press y - the from row's centre y): the rule reads the dragged row's centre, not the finger, so a row held by a handle off its centre is let go that much off (0 without a handle). Never on an edge: the shared reorder rule (shared/core/reorder_vectors.json rule.drag) passes a row when the dragged centre goes beyond its edge on the dragged row's side, the top of a row below and the bottom of a row above, as iOS 27's own reordering does; 3/4 and 1/4 of the to row are past its edge and short of the next.

list, when the case gives one, is the rect of the scrolling list that holds the rows (the nearest scrollable ancestor; none when the page or the window scrolls). Its visible part is list ∩ viewport. A row is on screen when its whole rect is inside the viewport and, with a list, inside the list's visible part (a lazy list clips a row the window would still show). On a platform whose lazy list does not create the rows it does not show (Android's LazyColumn), such a row is missing, not offscreen. The press and the release must each be at least listMargin from the top and the bottom of the list's visible part: the libraries' auto-scroll band (48, shared/core/reorder_vectors.json autoScroll) is measured from the list's edges, so a short list in the middle of the screen scrolls under a held finger far from the screen's edges.

Then the press and the release must each be at least edgeMargin from the viewport's top and bottom: nearer, a list scrolls by itself under a held finger (its own auto-scroll band) and the row lands further than `to`. Measured on iOS 27.2 (iPhone 17, a SwiftUI List with onMove, window 874 pt with the 34 pt home indicator): a release 129 pt above the window's bottom landed on `to`, one 55 pt above it moved the row two places further. The libraries' own bands are 48 (shared/core/reorder_vectors.json autoScroll).

canScrollUp / canScrollDown: whether the scroller that holds the rows (the list, or the page / window without one) can still scroll that way. The edge rule (both margins) applies on a side only when it can: a list at its top does not scroll under a finger held near its top, so its first row moves (and its last row at the bottom). Absent in a case means true (refuse when unsure). The web reads them exactly (scrollTop > 0; scrollTop + clientHeight < scrollHeight), and so does Android, from the list's scroll actions (Compose offers ScrollBy / scrolling towards a side only while it can scroll that way; a lazy list from its own canScrollBackward / canScrollForward): a list at its top reads (false, true), one whose header is cut off (true, true), a short list with no scrollable ancestor neither. iOS cannot read a list's offset and decides by the rows: up when <id>_item_0 is not found or not wholly inside the list's visible part; down when the last row found, counting up from the step's rows, is not wholly inside it. Its weak spot: content above row 0 or below the last row (a section header or footer) that is cut off is not seen, so a side is taken as not scrollable when it is.

verify: what the weak spot (and any scroll the plan missed) must not do is land the row elsewhere in silence. Before the gesture the driver records the frame of a row outside the moved range [min(from, to), max(from, to)] that is wholly on screen; such a row keeps its index and its place through a reorder. After the gesture the same row's top (y) must be within 1 of where it was; when it is not, the list scrolled under the finger, and the step fails: moveItem: the list scrolled during the drag ('<address>' moved by N); the row may have landed elsewhere — scroll the rows away from the list's edges first. When the row is no longer found at all (a lazy list scrolled it away and dropped it: after is null), the same sentence says ('<address>' moved off the screen) in place of moved by N. Only y is compared: v1 reorders one vertical column, so a scroll moves a row's top, while a row's x or size can change for other reasons (a row drawn shifted, raised or scaled while it settles) without the row landing elsewhere; N is how far its top moved. With no such row before the gesture the check is skipped.

fail names the first reason, in this order: same (from == to), section (section is not 0), ambiguous:<address>, missing:<address>, offscreen:<address> (from checked before to), no-handle (the case declares a handle and none was found in the from row), edge:<address> (the press's row, then the release's, too near the top or bottom of the screen or of the list's visible part).
timing: press the from point and hold pressSeconds, move to the release point slowly, hold holdSeconds, release.

verify.name: a row outside the moved range kept its place: no scroll
only x and the width changed: not a scroll
the same x and width change with the top moved by more than 1: scrolled
it moved: the list scrolled under the finger
